title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Plant Science (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Plant Science (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Plant Hormone is a naturally-occurring compound which regulates change in physiology, growth or development of the plant. Among the following which one is responsible to control dwarfness of the plant?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins (GA) are responsible for controlling dwarfness in plants.

questions.questionText: Plant cell type which are alive at maturity and have only a primary wall; provide mechanical support during growth?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living at maturity, have primary walls with uneven thickenings rich in pectin and hemicellulose, and provide mechanical support to growing plant parts. Sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity with thick secondary walls, while parenchyma cells are thin-walled and serve for storage and metabolism rather than primary mechanical support.

questions.questionText: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components in which the particle size is smaller than 1 nm. In which type of solutions the cell shrinks when it is placed in this solution?
questions.explanation: In hypertonic solutions, water moves out of the cell causing it to shrink.

questions.questionText: The minerals absorbed by the roots are mineral ions dissolved in the soil and water. They support plants to complete their life cycle and are to produce seeds. Which of the following is present in the green pigment of the leaf?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) is a central component of chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves.

questions.questionText: The rate at which water moves through the plants due to transpiration plays an important role in maintaining plant water balance. Which of the following is the instrument for measuring the rate of transpiration in plants?
questions.explanation: A potometer is used to measure the rate of water uptake (transpiration) in plants.

questions.questionText: Food preservation can be defined as the process of treating and handling food in such a way as to stop or greatly slow down spoilage and prevent foodborne illness while maintaining nutritional value, texture and flavor. Why is low temperature maintained for preservation?
questions.explanation: Low temperatures slow down bacterial growth, minimizing spoilage.

questions.questionText: What is an example of positive geotropism in plants?
questions.explanation: Positive geotropism (or gravitropism) is growth toward gravity, demonstrated by roots growing downward. Stems growing upward exhibit negative geotropism, lateral root growth is diagravitropism, and flower closing is a thigmotropic or nyctinastic response, not primarily gravitropic.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant Agronomist in commercial crop farms and the area is characterized by erratic rainfall you need to plan to get high production within drought situation, what is your plan to achieve the above goal?
options: Maintaining water balance by irrigation supplements
questions.explanation: All options are valid strategies for managing drought conditions.

questions.questionText: Simultaneous fusion of the generative nuclei one with egg cell and other with the endospermic nuclei is termed?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms where one sperm fertilizes the egg and another fertilizes the endosperm.

questions.questionText: The Rudimentary root of the seed or seedling that forms the primary root of the young plant is called as?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root that develops into the primary root.

questions.questionText: Seed is botanically called as?
questions.explanation: Botanically, a seed is a ripened ovule containing an embryo.

questions.questionText: The process of Seed drying is very important to maintain its?
questions.explanation: Proper seed drying is crucial for maintaining seed viability (ability to germinate) and vigor (strength and rate of germination). Excessive moisture in seeds accelerates deterioration through increased respiration, enzyme activity, and pathogen growth. Controlled drying to appropriate moisture content (typically 8-12% depending on species) extends storage life while preserving germination potential.

questions.questionText: A sound seed certification programme requires?
questions.explanation: Seed certification programs require legal frameworks (seed laws) to ensure quality standards.

questions.questionText: Free from inert matter and defective seeds are termed as?
questions.explanation: Physical purity refers to seeds free from inert matter and defective seeds.

questions.questionText: Possible reasons for seed dormancy is/are?
questions.explanation: All listed factors can contribute to seed dormancy.

questions.questionText: As you will be a Seed science expert in commercial fruit farms and you need to prepare seedlings form dormant seeds to your production site, what you will do?
questions.explanation: All methods (scarification, light treatment, stratification) can break seed dormancy.

questions.questionText: Primitive cultivars cultivated by farmers over generation and generation is known as?
questions.explanation: Land races are traditional varieties developed through generations of farmer selection.

questions.questionText: Single, Self-pollinated, homozygous plant is called as?
questions.explanation: A pure line is a homozygous, self-pollinated plant variety.

questions.questionText: Within an agricultural context drought is a prolonged period of deficit precipitation which results in negative impact on crop growth or yield. Among the following which one is the type of chemical which is accumulated when plants are under drought conditions?
questions.explanation: Proline is an amino acid that accumulates as an osmoprotectant during drought stress. It helps maintain cell turgor, stabilize proteins and cellular structures, and scavenge reactive oxygen species. Other compatible solutes that may accumulate during drought include glycine betaine and sugars. Plant hormones like abscisic acid also increase, while growth hormones like gibberellins, auxins, and cytokinins typically decrease during drought stress.

questions.questionText: Genetic Variation in clones may arise due to?
questions.explanation: All factors can introduce genetic variation in clones.

questions.questionText: Breeding for disease resistance requires
questions.explanation: All elements are necessary for successful disease resistance breeding.

questions.questionText: During hybridization how we can remove stamens from the flower bud?
questions.explanation: Emasculation is the removal of stamens to prevent self-pollination.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not used for crop improvement?
questions.explanation: Mutations are actually widely used for crop improvement. Natural and induced mutations create genetic variation that can be selected for desirable traits. The correct answer might have been intended to be something else, but all listed options are valid crop improvement methods.

questions.questionText: If water table is comparatively high, the irrigation canal becomes useless, due to?
options: Water logging of the cultivated areas
questions.explanation: High water tables cause multiple irrigation problems.

questions.questionText: The main cause of silting up a channel is?
questions.explanation: All factors contribute to channel silting.

questions.questionText: Pick up the correct statement from the following?
options: Gravity water is harmful to crops
Hygroscopic water remains attached to soil molecules by chemical bond
Capillary moisture held in the soil pores against gravity by surface tension, is utilized by plants
questions.explanation: Capillary water is available for plant uptake.

questions.questionText: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following?
options: In free flooding irrigation, water is admitted at one corner of a field and is allowed to spread over the entire area
In check method of irrigation, the field is divided into smaller compartments and water is admitted to each in turn
In furrow irrigation water is admitted between the rows of plants in the field
questions.explanation: All statements about irrigation methods are correct.

questions.questionText: A fall in a canal bed is generally provided, if
options: Ground slope exceeds the designed bed slope
Designed bed slope exceeds the ground slope
Ground slope is practically the same as the designed bed slope
questions.explanation: Falls are needed when ground slope exceeds designed slope to control water velocity.

questions.questionText: Effective precipitation for a crop may be defined as?
options: Total precipitation minus the loss due to evaporation
Total precipitation minus the loss due to infiltration
Total precipitation during the crop period
Available water stored in soil within root zone of the crop
questions.explanation: Effective precipitation is the water actually available to crops in the root zone.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The canal system and the drainage system are complementary
The canal system runs on ridges, gets divided into smaller channels and spreads its water on the land
The drainage system runs along the lowest line, collects drainage water from the slopes and joins the main stream
questions.explanation: All statements about irrigation and drainage systems are correct.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the chemical which is used for killing unwanted weeds?
questions.explanation: Herbicides are specifically designed to control weeds.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is false about weeds?
options: Weeds are pests and guest plants
Parasitic weeds are independent on the soils to grow
All weeds have no beneficial effect for other
questions.explanation: Some weeds can have beneficial effects, such as providing habitat for beneficial insects, preventing soil erosion, contributing organic matter to soil, or having medicinal properties. Many weeds that are considered 'nuisance plants' in one context may have ecological or economic value in other contexts.

questions.questionText: Biology of weeds which deals about?
options: The interaction between weeds and their environment
The classification of weeds based on their origin
questions.explanation: Weed biology focuses on weed-environment interactions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the method of classifying weeds morphologically?
options: Based on the impact of the environmental effects of the animals
Based on plant structure (e.g., grasses vs broadleaves)
questions.explanation: Morphological classification is based on physical characteristics.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is not encourage the establishment and survival of weeds?
questions.explanation: Good agronomic practices suppress weeds.

questions.questionText: Inhibition of a plant's growth due to the release of bio-chemicals in the environment is?
questions.explanation: Allelopathy involves biochemical inhibition of plant growth.

questions.questionText: The minimum period of time during which the crop must be free of weeds in order to prevent loss in yield is?
questions.explanation: This critical period determines when weed control is most crucial.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about modern tillage?
questions.explanation: 'Many tillage' is not a recognized modern tillage practice.

questions.questionText: Crops grown and plowed under while still green in order to improve soil fertility is?
questions.explanation: Green manure crops are incorporated to enrich soil fertility.

questions.questionText: Ability of seeds to germinate under optimal conditions is?
questions.explanation: Viability refers to seed germination potential.

questions.questionText: All of the following crops are two seasonal, except one?
questions.explanation: Wheat is typically a single-season crop.

questions.questionText: Of the following statements, which one is not true about pulse crops?
options: Their seeds are rich in protein
questions.explanation: Pulse crops typically exhibit epigeal germination, where the cotyledons emerge above ground (not hypogeal where cotyledons remain below ground). Examples like beans, chickpeas, and lentils demonstrate epigeal germination, making the statement 'They are hypogal during germination' false.

questions.questionText: An irreversible increase in size, volume or mass of a cell or organ or whole organisms?
questions.explanation: Growth is defined as irreversible increase in size/mass.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is not major cereal crop of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Soybean is a legume, not a cereal crop.

questions.questionText: Which experimental design involves main plots and sub-plots in its layout?
questions.explanation: Split plot designs have nested treatments (main plots and subplots).

questions.questionText: One of the following is not source of variation of RCBD?
questions.explanation: Columns aren't a standard source of variation in RCBD.

questions.questionText: Which of the following experimental design is most widely used in field?
questions.explanation: RCBD is most common for field experiments due to blocking.

questions.questionText: What is the value of an 'A' in the ANOVA table?
questions.explanation: In the ANOVA table, 'A' represents the Error Sum of Squares, calculated as Total SS - (Block SS + Treatment SS) = 30.45 - (15 + 10) = 5.45.

questions.questionText: Calculated value of 'D' is?
questions.explanation: Error DF = Total DF - (Block DF + Treatment DF) = 15 - (3 + 3) = 9.

questions.questionText: Which one is the calculated value of F?
questions.explanation: F = Treatment MS / Error MS = (10/3)/(5.45/9) ≈ 3.33.

questions.questionText: What the least significant difference (LSD) of the study?
questions.explanation: The LSD is calculated using the formula: LSD = t(α/2, df) × √(2 × MSE/r), where t is the critical t-value, MSE is the mean square error, and r is the number of replications. Given the information available, 1.24 is the correct LSD value.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is true?
options: High temperature increase the rate of water loss in vegetable crops
Vegetable products must be stored at high RH (>90%) except: root and tuber crops (RH=50 - 60%)
The temperature at which maximum storage is attained varies from product to product
questions.explanation: All statements about vegetable storage are correct.

questions.questionText: A science dealing with cultivation, harvesting, post-harvest handling, processing and marketing of vegetable crops?
questions.explanation: Olericulture is the science of vegetable production.

questions.questionText: Which vegetables are growing under the ground?
questions.explanation: Root/tuber crops grow underground.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is the importance of vegetables storage?
options: To ensure regular supply of seasonal produce all year round
Preservation of nutritional quality and weapon for national stability
questions.explanation: All options describe benefits of vegetable storage.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant science production expert in commercial vegetable farms and you need to prepare seedlings for your production site, what is your consideration for vegetable nursery site selection?
questions.explanation: Soil quality and water availability are critical for nurseries.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All matches are actually correct: Sweet potato is a root crop (modified storage roots), Tomato is botanically a fruit vegetable, Onion is a bulb crop, and Cabbage is a leafy vegetable. The question may have been intended to ask which is 'incorrectly' matched, but as written, all options are valid classifications.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the opportunities for vegetables production in Ethiopia?
options: The presence of favorable agro-ecological conditions for successful growing of various fruit crops
Proximity of the country to fertile markets of Europe and Middle East Asia
questions.explanation: All factors present opportunities for Ethiopian vegetable production.

questions.questionText: Which method of classification is very helpful for botanist and breeder who are interested to study morphology, cross ability and taxonomic character?
options: Classification based on nature and structure of ovary wall
questions.explanation: Botanical classification is most useful for taxonomic studies.

questions.questionText: Banana is commercially propagated by?
questions.explanation: Sword suckers are the preferred banana propagation material.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is a post-harvest practice accomplished by flooding spraying or immersing the produce by water?
questions.explanation: Hydrocooling uses water immersion for rapid cooling.

questions.questionText: Which is not applicable to vegetatively propagated fruits?
options: To get true to type plants
To get a new type of plant
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation maintains existing genotypes, doesn't create new ones.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is pre-condition required for establishment of orchards?
questions.explanation: All steps are necessary for orchard establishment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All climate-fruit pairings are correct.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant science production manager in large scale fruit farm and you need to expand the area of production site, what is your consideration for that purpose?
questions.explanation: All factors (temperature, soil, water availability, and market access) are critical considerations for orchard expansion. Market access is particularly important for commercial viability, but a comprehensive approach would consider all these factors together for successful expansion.

questions.questionText: Which one is an approach for searching new facts through organized scientific investigation?
questions.explanation: Research is systematic investigation to discover new knowledge.

questions.questionText: Which one the following is a purpose of a research?
options: to provide solution for complex problems
questions.explanation: Both problem-solving and hypothesis testing are research purposes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following terms well define qualitative data?
questions.explanation: Qualitative data is characterized by being non-numerical, descriptive, and often used in anthropological and sociological research. It includes observations that can be described but not precisely measured numerically. Options B and C both describe aspects of qualitative data, making 'All except A' the correct comprehensive answer.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct steps for scientific research?
options: problem identification- analysis- data collection- reviewing information
drawing conclusion – analysis – data collection – problem identification
problem identification – reviewing information – data collection – analysis – drawing conclusion
questions.explanation: This sequence represents the standard scientific method.

questions.questionText: The written document for the requesting both authorization and funds to undertake a specific project in a laboratory, library or field is called?
questions.explanation: A research proposal seeks approval and funding.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not an outline of research proposal?
questions.explanation: Results come after proposal approval, not in the proposal itself.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an assumption or guesses about the relationship between two research variable?
questions.explanation: A hypothesis predicts relationships between variables.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an abiotic factor for the development of a plant disease?
questions.explanation: Weather is a non-living (abiotic) disease factor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a symptom of diseased plant?
questions.explanation: All options describe plant disease symptoms.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the scanting pattern of disease assessment in the field?
questions.explanation: All patterns are used for field disease assessment.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is an organism that man regards as a harmful to his personal properties or environment?
questions.explanation: Pests are organisms harmful to human interests.

questions.questionText: Of the following one is defined as the physical harm or distraction to a valued commodity caused by the presence of activity of a pest?
questions.explanation: Damage refers to actual harm caused by pests.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are the major pillars of disease triangle?
options: Resistant Host- a virulent pathogen – none conducting environment
Susceptible Host – virulent pathogen – conducive environment
questions.explanation: Disease requires susceptible host, virulent pathogen, and favorable environment.

questions.questionText: The use of living organism that are predators to control pest is called?
questions.explanation: Biological control uses natural predators/parasites.

questions.questionText: Which one is not an example of a relative method to assess economic threshold levels for an insect pest is?
questions.explanation: All are relative assessment methods.

questions.questionText: The honey bee waggle dance conveys information about the location of nectar sources to other worker bees in the hive. Which of the following senses do worker bees use to interpret the dance?
questions.explanation: Honey bees use multiple senses to interpret the waggle dance, but primarily rely on sight and touch. They observe the dancing bee visually and also detect vibrations and movements through touch receptors. The direction of the dance indicates the direction of the food source relative to the sun, while the duration of the waggle run indicates distance. Smell also plays a role as dancers often carry the scent of the food source.

questions.questionText: An example of a biological control against insects is?
questions.explanation: Pheromones (sex hormones) are used in biological control.

questions.questionText: Which insect orders contain species that are important pests of domestic animals?
questions.explanation: All listed orders contain livestock pests.

questions.questionText: Which control strategy is likely to have the greatest impact on non-target organisms?
questions.explanation: Chemical control methods (pesticides) often have broader effects beyond the target pest, affecting beneficial insects, soil microorganisms, aquatic life, and even wildlife. These non-target impacts occur through direct toxicity, bioaccumulation, or habitat disruption. Cultural, biological, and physical controls are generally more selective and have fewer impacts on non-target organisms.

questions.questionText: Which orders are most important in the transmission of human disease?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes (Diptera) and lice (Phthiraptera) transmit many diseases.

questions.questionText: Chitin is most abundant in which part of the exoskeleton?
questions.explanation: Chitin, a polysaccharide that provides structural support in arthropod exoskeletons, is most abundant in the procuticle layer. The procuticle consists of two parts: the exocuticle (outer, harder layer) and endocuticle (inner, more flexible layer), both containing chitin-protein complexes. The epicuticle is the outermost waxy layer containing no chitin, while the epidermis is the living cell layer beneath the cuticle that secretes the exoskeletal components.

questions.questionText: Plant biotechnology involves?
options: Production of valuable products in plants
rapid clonal multiplication of desired genotypes
questions.explanation: All are applications of plant biotechnology.

questions.questionText: The most common solidifying agent used in micro propagation is?
questions.explanation: Agar is the standard gelling agent for media.

questions.questionText: The culturing of cells in liquid agitated medium is called?
questions.explanation: Suspension cultures grow cells in liquid medium with agitation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is best suited method for production of virus free plants?
questions.explanation: Meristem culture exploits virus-free apical meristems.

questions.questionText: Gene silencing is generally termed as?
questions.explanation: Gene silencing refers to suppressing gene expression.

questions.questionText: The production of adventitious roots and shoots from cells of tissue culture is termed?
questions.explanation: Organogenesis is de novo organ formation in vitro.

questions.questionText: Protoplast fusion and somatic hybridization in plant are based on which the following?
questions.explanation: All steps are involved in somatic hybridization.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about the specific objectives of the Soil Fertility and Plant Nutrition?
options: To describe how plants take up or absorb nutrients
Identify and describe plant nutrients deficiency symptoms
Describe how soil organic matter, C.E.C, PH, affect nutrient availability
questions.explanation: All the listed objectives (describing nutrient uptake mechanisms, identifying deficiency symptoms, understanding soil properties affecting nutrient availability, and evaluating soil amendments) are valid objectives in soil fertility and plant nutrition studies. None of the individual statements is untrue, so the answer is 'all' - meaning all statements are true objectives of soil fertility and plant nutrition.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not Macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Mn and Zn are micronutrients.

questions.questionText: Among the following one is the capacity to produce a certain yield of crops or other plants with optimum management?
questions.explanation: Soil productivity refers to yield potential under management.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about theory of Liebig (1803-1873)?
options: for the first time he gave a theory about soil fertility and plant nutrition
Carbon for plants from CO₂ of atmosphere
Hydrogen and oxygen for plant comes from water
Phosphorus is necessary for seed formation
Crops require both P and K
questions.explanation: Liebig's Law of the Minimum didn't specify P+K requirement.

questions.questionText: Which one is the most concentrated form of phosphate, which is required by plants?
questions.explanation: Calcium dihydrogen phosphate is a plant-available P form.

questions.questionText: The term Actinomycetes refers?
options: conversion of organic Phosphorus compounds to inorganic
conversion of inorganic Phosphorus to organic Phosphorus
break down of P into soil over a long period of time
group of bacteria with a superficial resemblance to fungi
dissolve of Solid P minerals in the soil in to the soil solution
questions.explanation: Actinomycetes are a group of filamentous bacteria that superficially resemble fungi. They play important roles in decomposition of organic materials in soil and can produce antibiotics. While they can contribute to nutrient cycling including phosphorus, their definition is specifically about their morphology and taxonomy.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the dissolved forms of plant-available P in the soil solution?
questions.explanation: Orthophosphate ions (H2PO4-, HPO42-) are plant-available P forms.
